questions.question: What are useful Rails console tricks?
questions.title: Rails Console Tricks
questions.direct_answer: The Rails console (rails c) loads your app so you can try models and code live. Useful tricks: rails c --sandbox rolls back DB changes on exit (safe experimentation); app object (app.get '/posts/42'; app.response.body) hits routes without a server; reload! reloads your code after edits (pick up changes without restarting); _ holds the last result; helper object accesses view helpers (helper.number_to_currency(10)); controller methods; User.all, Post.create!(...) interact with the DB. For long sessions, require 'pry' and binding.pry for deeper inspection. The console is the fastest way to test a query, a method, or a migration result without writing a test or hitting the browser.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know rails c --sandbox (rollback), reload!, the app object, and _ for the last result.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Running rails c without --sandbox and mutating the DB (use --sandbox for experiments), or forgetting reload! after editing code.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: rails c loads your app live. --sandbox rolls back DB changes; reload! picks up edits; app hits routes; _ = last result; helper for view helpers.

sections.title: Console Tricks
sections.content:
rails c --sandbox (rollback); reload!; app (hit routes); _ (last result); helper.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[rails c] --> S[--sandbox: rollback on exit]
  C --> R[reload!: pick up edits]
  C --> A[app.get '/x'; app.response.body]
  C --> U[_ = last result; helper]
```

sections.title: Rails console tricks
sections.content:
```ruby
# Start the console:
#   rails c                 # load app + DB
#   rails c --sandbox        # DB changes ROLL BACK on exit (safe)

reload!              # reload your code after editing (no restart needed)
_                   # the last result
User.all            # query the DB live
Post.create!(title: 'x')   # create (bang raises on validation fail)

# `app` hits routes without a server:
app.get '/posts/42'
app.response.body          # the response body
app.response.status        # the status code

# `helper` accesses view helpers:
helper.number_to_currency(10)   # "$10.00"
helper.pluralize(2, 'post')     # '2 posts'

# Try a method quickly:
post = Post.last
post.excerpt               # call a model method live

# `binding.pry` inside console -> drop into pry for deeper inspection.
# Fastest way to test a query/method/migration without a browser or a test.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Running rails c without --sandbox and mutating the DB (use --sandbox for experiments).
Forgetting reload! after editing code (changes won't apply until reload).
Using the console to test permanent data (use --sandbox; or a test).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: rails c loads your app; rails c --sandbox rolls back DB changes on exit.
reload! reloads your code after edits (pick up changes without restarting).
The app object hits routes without a server (app.get; app.response.body).
_ holds the last result; helper accesses view helpers (helper.number_to_currency).
It's the fastest way to test a query/method/migration result without a browser.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: The Rails console (rails c) loads your app so you can try models and code live. Useful tricks: rails c dash dash sandbox rolls back DB changes on exit (safe experimentation); app object (app dot get posts 42; app dot response dot body) hits routes without a server; reload! reloads your code after edits (pick up changes without restarting); underscore holds the last result; helper object accesses view helpers (helper dot number_to_currency 10); controller methods; User dot all, Post dot create interact with the DB. For long sessions, require pry and binding dot pry for deeper inspection. The console is the fastest way to test a query, a method, or a migration result without writing a test or hitting the browser. A common mistake is running rails c without sandbox and mutating the DB, when you should use sandbox for experiments, and forgetting reload after editing code.
